messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update the existing train mystery game so customization and case information overlay a full-width carriage scene, and make exploration a playable movement experience with passenger interactions, door transitions, and walking animations.

## Requirements
- Keep the entire train car visible across the horizontal game screen.
- Make the character move through the environment and use doors to travel between cars.
- Give each passenger a distinct interaction approach.
- Animate the character and pet while walking.
- Build on the existing game without clarification.

## Decisions
- Retained the single-file pixel-art game and made the interface a floating overlay.
- Added keyboard, click-to-move, and touch controls; E/Enter interacts, and C toggles the casebook.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated `index.html` layout for a full-screen carriage with overlay panel and responsive touch controls.
- Added movement state/update loop, step bob animations for the detective and pet, carriage-door visuals, proximity prompts, and per-passenger introductions.

### Active
- Validate and fix the changes; no browser check or test has been run yet.

### Blocked
- The game logic has likely incomplete/incorrect event wiring and needs verification before considering the build playable.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` for syntax/runtime issues, especially `drawCharacter`, the CSS for `.case-button` / `show-case`, and the interaction handlers.
2. Ensure door interaction is reachable and only transitions at the appropriate edge; verify passenger and clue interactions and panel visibility.
3. Run the game in a browser, test keyboard/touch movement and transitions, then capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Single-file game; contains layout, rendering, UI, and all gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- New controls include `#touchPad`, `#caseToggle`, and movement via arrows/WASD; `E` or Enter triggers nearby interaction.
- Existing `setCar()` still permits wrapping among three cars, and the play button now displays a prompt instead of directly advancing during play.

## Objective
- Update the existing train mystery game so customization and case information overlay a full-width carriage scene, with playable movement, passenger interactions, door transitions, and walking animations.

## Requirements
- Keep the entire train car visible across the horizontal game screen.
- Make the character move through the environment and use doors to travel between cars.
- Give each passenger a distinct interaction approach.
- Animate the character and pet while walking.
- Build on the existing game without clarification.

## Decisions
- Retained the single-file pixel-art game and made the interface a floating overlay.
- Added keyboard, click-to-move, and touch controls; E/Enter interacts, and C toggles the casebook.
- The play button prompts the player to walk to a carriage door and press E rather than advancing cars directly.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated `index.html` for a full-screen carriage with a floating customization/casebook panel and responsive touch controls.
- Added movement state/update loop, step animations, carriage-door visuals, proximity prompts, and per-passenger introductions.
- Added casebook toggle styling and verified it appears during play while the customization panel hides.
- Extracted the inline script and confirmed it passes `node --check`.
- Opened the game in Chromium; screenshots showed the carriage scene and playing state, and the browser console had no errors.
- Verified keyboard movement and door interaction can transition carriages.

### Active
- Validate casebook toggle, passenger and clue interactions, carriage door transitions, ending state, and mobile controls.
- Review/fix any visual or gameplay issues found during testing.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test casebook open/close during play and ensure the overlay does not interfere with movement or dialogue.
2. Test passenger introductions, clue collection, traversal among all three cars, and the ending.
3. Test responsive touch controls and inspect a recent screenshot; fix any issues found.
4. Re-run JavaScript syntax validation after changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Single-file game containing layout, rendering, UI, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Car transitions wrap among three cars.
- Browser testing is available through `playwright-cli`; the local game was served at `http://localhost:3002`.
